title: Half-wave and full-wave rectifiers: turning AC into DC with diodes
examples: How does a bridge rectifier work?

parts.label: Diode
parts.ask: How does a half-wave rectifier work?

explain.say: The socket gives AC, but your phone's battery needs DC, current that flows one way only. The first step in every charger is a rectifier. On the board, a transformer gives 12 volts RMS, about 17 volts peak, and a single diode feeds a 1 kilohm load. Let's see what the load receives.

draw.text: Half-wave and full-wave rectifiers: turning AC into DC with diodes

parts.label: Diode
parts.ask: How does a half-wave rectifier work?

explain.say: On the positive half of each cycle the diode is forward biased and conducts, so the load sees the input minus the diode's 0.7 volts, peaking at 16.3 volts. On the negative half the diode blocks, and the load gets nothing. Only half of each wave gets through: a half-wave rectifier. Is the output DC now?

curves.label: Half-wave out
curves.ask: How does a half-wave rectifier work?

curves.label: Full-wave out
curves.ask: What is the ripple frequency of a full-wave rectifier?

explain.say: Sort of: it flows one way, but in bumps with gaps. Its average, the DC value a meter would read, is the peak over pi: 16.3 over 3.14, about 5.2 volts. Half the time, the transformer does nothing useful, and the bumps come only 50 times a second, which is hard to smooth. Can you think of a way to use the negative halves too?

curves.ask: How does a half-wave rectifier work?

curves.label: Full-wave out
curves.ask: What is the ripple frequency of a full-wave rectifier?

explain.say: Flip them over! A bridge of four diodes does exactly that. On each half cycle, two of the diodes conduct and steer the current through the load in the same direction. The cost is two diode drops in the path, so the peak is 17 minus 1.4, which is 15.6 volts. Which diodes conduct on the negative half?

parts.label: Diode bridge
parts.ask: How does a bridge rectifier work?

parts.label: Load
parts.ask: Why is the bridge output peak lower?

draw.text: Bridge: one pair of diodes conducts on each half cycle, in turn.

explain.say: The other pair. Now look at the full-wave curve: a bump every half cycle, 100 times a second. The average doubles to 2 times the peak over pi, about 9.9 volts, and the faster bumps are much easier to smooth. Great work! Exam tip: each diode must survive the peak reverse voltage, about 17 volts here, so pick its rating with margin. Challenge: what average would a 24 volt RMS bridge give?

faq.a: A circuit that converts AC into DC, current flowing in one direction only, using diodes as one-way valves.
asks: How do you convert AC to DC?

faq.q: How does a half-wave rectifier work?
faq.a: A single diode conducts on the positive half cycles and blocks the negative ones, so the load gets only the positive halves. Its average output is about the peak over pi.

faq.q: How does a bridge rectifier work?
faq.a: Four diodes are arranged so that on each half cycle a different pair conducts, always steering current the same way through the load. Both halves of the wave are used.

faq.q: Why is the bridge output peak lower?
faq.a: Current passes through two diodes in series on every half cycle, so two drops of about 0.7 volts are lost: 17 volts becomes about 15.6 volts.
asks: Why a 1.4 V drop in a bridge rectifier?

faq.q: What is the ripple frequency of a full-wave rectifier?
faq.a: Twice the supply frequency, because there is a bump every half cycle: 100 hertz on a 50 hertz supply, and 120 hertz on a 60 hertz supply.

facts: A full-wave rectifier's average output is twice that of a half-wave rectifier with the same peak.
On a 50 hertz supply, a full-wave rectifier delivers 100 bumps per second.

quiz.say: A half-wave rectifier gives a peak output of 31.4 volts. What is its average DC output?
quiz.show: A half-wave rectifier gives a peak output of 31.4 V. What is its average DC output?
quiz.why: The half-wave average is the peak over pi: 31.4 over 3.14 is 10 volts.

wrong.1: Twice the peak over pi is the full-wave average.
wrong.2: That is the peak over root 2, the RMS of a full sine wave.

quiz.say: How many diodes conduct at the same time in a bridge rectifier?
quiz.show: How many diodes conduct at the same time in a bridge rectifier?
quiz.why: On each half cycle one opposite pair conducts, so two at a time.

wrong.1: One diode at a time is the half-wave circuit.
wrong.2: If all four conducted together they would short the supply.
